item.title: Why Bengals-Steelers is the biggest game at Paycor Stadium in years
item.description: Paycor Stadium hasn't seen a game like this coming weekend's Cincinnati Bengals-Pittsburgh Steelers AFC North showdown in quite some time. Pretty much every NFL game is "big" and important to some degree, but over the last three years, "big" in Cincinnati has taken the shape of the Bengals dropping their most-anticipated contests. Or they're fighting to climb back into the AFC playoff picture after a slow start. On Sunday, Nov. 16, the Bengals host the Steelers in what could be one of the most-anticipated games in Paycor Stadium history: A Week 10, Sunday Night Football , primetime affair between two 6-2 rivals with first place in the AFC North on the line. Suffice it to say games of this magnitude have been rare during the Cincinnati's three-season playoff drought. "This is as big of a game as we've had here for a while," Burrow said. "We lost to them early in the season. So number one, with the standings at the end of the year, you want that to be split. And number two, for first place outright. And so, like you said, huge game." The Steelers on Sept. 27 narrowly defeated the Bengals at Acrisure Stadium, 30-27, and forced a turnover on Cincinnati's final drive to avoid overtime, or worse. When's the last time the Bengals hosted a game of this relative magnitude at Paycor Stadium? Let's see. Does last season's Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears meet that standard? The Bengals were 3-5 entering the game and 3-6 afterward. Most of the games after that point became about draft order. How about the 2024 season? In Week 17 that year, Cincinnati beat the Denver Broncos in overtime. But the win only brought the late-charging Bengals back to .500 at 8-8. They finished the year at 9-8 but were always a longshot to reach the postseason after a slow start to the season. Realistically, you're reaching back to the 2022 season to find anything comparable to the next edition of Bengals-Steelers. The teams' second meeting of 2026 has several characteristics that could make it a classic, too. There's the Aaron Rodgers-versus-Burrow quarterback matchup, to the primetime TV time slot, to the weather as some forecasts call for temperatures to drop below 40F as the game progresses. Burrow contended one win wouldn't decide the outcome of the AFC North, but breaking the Bengals-Steelers deadlock atop the division could actually be very determinative. Looking beyond this game, Cincinnati has just three games remaining against teams that currently have a winning record (two games against the Cleveland Browns (5-4), one against Kansas City Chiefs (6-2). The Steelers have two games against winning teams left on the schedule following their trip to Cincinnati (Denver Broncos (7-2), Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2). That being said, neither team can afford to take anyone likely, including the teams with losing records. item.title: Ja’Marr Chase says 2026 Bengals are better than 2021 Super Bowl team
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals superstar wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done a lot of winning in his football career and has been a part of many talented teams at different levels. From playing in the LHSAA Division I state championship game his sophomore season, to winning the NCAA National Championship in 2019 to going to the Super Bowl in 2021, he’s been on fantastic teams. He says the 2026 Bengals are the best. When Chase was asked if the 6-2 Bengals are the best Bengals team he’s played for, he said yes, and it’s not particularly close. “I would say, by far [this team is the best Bengals team I’ve played on],” he told Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer on Tuesday . “I know we went to the Super Bowl. We had a good run with those guys. This is another great group we have… Honestly, I think the whole team is one unit.” The Bengals’ improbable Super Bowl run following the 2021 season, and their narrow loss in the AFC Championship game the following season, were their last two playoff appearances. After three straight seasons of no playoff football, and a roster turnover on the defensive side of the ball, the Bengals are hoping to get back to the postseason once the 2026 regular season comes to an end. Burrow and the offense have put up staggering numbers over the last three weeks. If that trend continues, the sky’s the limit. What do you think? Are the 2026 Bengals better than the 2021 squad?

Bryant swung a mishit on the following play as well. That sequence was part of the Nittany Lions’ four-point run. While the Terps clawed back in the set, they couldn’t overtake Penn State. item.title: How Nia Hislop found her voice as a UMass women's soccer leader
item.description: NOTE : UMass journalism students teamed up with MassLive to take readers inside the UMass women’s soccer program, highlighting the players, coaches and stories that make the Minutewomen special. Through a series of features, students explore the people and perseverance behind a team that has its sights set on a successful postseason run. UMass heads into the MAC semifinals Tuesday, Nov. 10, looking to take another step toward a conference championship. In 1999, Shaka Hislop made his debut for Trinidad and Tobago’s men’s national soccer team at Hasely Crawford Stadium in Port of Spain. Seven years later, he helped the country reach its first World Cup. On April 17, 2026, nearly three decades after his own debut, Hislop watched his daughter take the same field, wearing the colors of Trinidad and Tobago for the first time. For Nia Hislop, a UMass women’s soccer captain, it was more than a national team debut. It was a chance to follow in her father’s footsteps, represent her family’s homeland and begin a new chapter in a journey that had already taken plenty of twists. “The first time I touched the ball, or I did something good, the stadium was so loud,” Nia Hislop said. “I was like, oh my God, this is legit.” As she stepped onto the moss-green field as a 62nd-minute substitute, she scanned the crowd for her family amid an ocean of passionate Trinidadian supporters. A section of roughly 30 friends and family members cheered, wearing shirts with “Hislop” printed across the back. Her mother, Desha, broke into tears of joy. Her father, Shaka, sat beside her and tried to take in the moment without breaking down himself. “It invoked so many emotions in me,” Shaka said. “Seeing [Nia], she came off the bench to come on and play. Just as a dad ... I held it together. But above all, I wanted that moment to be about her and her journey in this game and everything that it meant to her through the years.” UMass captain Nia Hislop (32) dribbles the ball during action earlier this season at Rudd Field in Amherst. Photo by Trang Nguyen At home, her siblings exchanged excited texts, sharing pictures of their sister on the television screen. In Amherst, Massachusetts, her college teammates screamed at the television, recording their reactions to send to Nia after the match. UMass women’s soccer coach Jason Dowiak also watched the moment unfold from his couch at home. “I was taking videos of it and sending it to my friends, and I was like, ‘That’s my girl, that’s my girl,’” Dowiak said. Her national team debut marked a significant milestone in Nia’s return to the field after a season-ending hip injury forced her to miss the 2025 collegiate campaign. item.title: Red Sox’s Craig Breslow Hints at ‘Sweeping’ Changes Inside Organization
item.description: With the Trade Deadline looming, a question of trust hangs over the Boston Red Sox and CBO Craig Breslow. Getty To say the Boston Red Sox dealt with the injury bug in 2026 would be an understatement. Star players such as outfielder Roman Anthony and ace Garrett Crochet spent significant time on the injured list with little to no communication between the organization and the general public. Especially with Anthony, even the team didn’t seem to fully understand the injury. Now, Craig Breslow has decided to add some accountability to the Red Sox. According to MassLive’s Christopher Smith, the organization is taking a longer look at its medical department and how it should best function moving forward. What Did Boston Red Sox CBO Craig Breslow Say? While Boston made the playoffs after a horrific start to the season that included firing manager Alex Cora, injuries and communication remained at the forefront of everyone’s mind. “We’re constantly assessing ‘what are we getting right, what are we getting wrong, what are the opportunities to improve,’” Breslow told Smith. “And I think it’s important to try and decouple — are we getting the diagnosis or the rehab wrong, or do we need to make sure that communication with our players, with our staff internally, with the media externally is tightened up? And so we’re going to evaluate all those things this offseason and definitely recognize where some of the criticism is coming from.​” Every team obviously deals with injuries throughout a major league season. However, to see a team so shorthanded and have no communication with the fans is disappointing. The Red Sox’ medical staff had several gaffes this season where the issue was misdiagnosed or was more of a problem than expected. Examples of Why There Needs to Be Change Reliever Garrett Whitlock underwent testing at the end of the season that found he was pitching on a fractured tibia. The Red Sox only diagnosed the injury after recurring leg pain forced more imaging. As for Boston’s ace, several setbacks kept Crochet sidelined from April 26 to Boston’s Wild Card series. But the most notable gaffe of all was Anthony’s injury. Interim manager Chad Tracy expected Anthony to be day-to-day with a wrist injury. That ailment would keep him out for over 100 games (until August 30) and forced him to miss postseason time. Boston cleared Anthony to play. However, he was dealing with pain throughout his return, making the decision questionable at best. While Breslow acknowledged that Anthony and Crochet will be ready for next season, these misdiagnoses altered Boston’s season permanently. “We’re going to take kind of a sweeping look at a number of our processes and make sure that we are diagnosing injuries the best we possibly can,” Breslow said. Breslow needs to make changes if Boston doesn’t want history to repeat itself. item.title: LSU gymnastics inks top recruiting class, five defer for Olympics
item.description: On Wednesday, the LSU gymnastics team signed 10 recruits to the classes of 2027 and 2028 which formed the top recruiting class in the nation. Last year, LSU got commitments from nine gymnasts, a number which shocked most people considering the new roster limits. Those who’d been paying attention, as well as those who read my coverage, would know that the size would make sense once the class split. This signing day made that split clearer. In the class of 2027, LSU signed Myla Ruck, Jada Oliver, Kiari Sparks, Sage Bradford and Josie Lynch. These five will be part of the 2028 team. Five others announced that they’d be signing and also deferring their enrollment by a year to train for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Hezly Rivera joined the nine who committed in 2025 in signing with LSU, and Team USA hopefuls Tatum Drusch and Reese Esponda joined her in signing and deferring. As I speculated, Canadian elites Lia Redick and Zoé Cadrin are also deferring their enrollment to try and earn a spot on their country’s national team. Those five will join LSU for the 2029 season. LSU hasn’t finished looking for recruits in the 2028 recruiting class. On Saturday, they hosted American elite standouts Charleigh Bullock and Caroline Moreau, the latter of which seemed to really enjoy her time based on the three TikToks she made head coach Jay Clark do. LSU has room to add both without much issue right now.

item.title: Traded MN Twins Pitcher Wins Reliever of the Year
item.description: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect This season, the Minnesota Twins finished with a 77-85 record . They were largely sunk by a bullpen that couldn’t keep games together after their starter departed. Of course, that group was depleted at the trade deadline during the 2025 season. Tom Pohlad and Jeremy Zoll opted against rebuilding it during the offseason. It made sense to trade expiring relief assets from a team that ultimately finished with a 70-92 record . It didn’t make much sense to part out future assets for pennies on the dollar. That’s what the MN Twins did with hometown talent Louis Varland, though. Now, less than two years later, he’s won an award as the best reliever in the American League. Louis Varland finds new heights away from MN Twins A former 15th-round pick, Louis Varland found success in the Minnesota Twins bullpen.
